notes: **Absolute expansion:** the real increase in volume of a liquid when heated, measured without any container. $\Delta V_{abs} = V_0 \gamma_{liq} \Delta T$.
**Apparent expansion:** the observed increase in volume of a liquid when heated in a container, which also expands. $\Delta V_{app} = V_0(\gamma_{liq} - \gamma_{glass})\Delta T$.
**Why apparent is less than absolute:** the container expands, so the scale marks move outward, making the liquid level rise seem smaller than the actual volume increase.
**Practical consequence:** a mercury thermometer reads correctly only because the glass expansion is accounted for in calibration.
**Anomalous expansion of water:** water contracts from 0Â°C to 4Â°C, then expands above 4Â°C. This is why ice floats and ponds freeze from the top down.
